narrative:
On August 28, 2026, the Karnataka High Court resolved 1,102 cases out of 2,611 scheduled hearings across 69 judges, achieving an overall hearing rate of 42.2%. This conversion rate represents an efficiency increase from the 36.8% recorded on August 14 and the 38.1% on July 31, though it remains below the peak of 44.5% observed on August 3. 

In terms of stages, Orders dominated the docket with 909 scheduled matters, achieving a 45.4% hearing rate. Admission stages converted 43.8% of 521 scheduled cases, while Preliminary Hearings saw a stronger clearance rate of 51.2%. Final Hearings, which have historically recorded lower conversion rates, such as 17.7% on August 14 and 16.5% on August 3, saw moderate improvement today at 25.1% of 502 scheduled cases. 

Case-type distribution reveals that Writ Petitions (WP) made up the largest share of the workload with 995 scheduled matters, converting 39.6% into active hearings. Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) and Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) performed similarly, with hearing rates of 44.2% and 44.0% respectively. Regular Second Appeals (RSA) demonstrated the highest efficiency among major case categories, with 61.6% of 164 scheduled matters being heard.

Judge-wise performance highlights varied across courtrooms. Justice V. Srishananda in Court Hall 21 managed a high-volume docket exceptionally well, hearing 75 out of 104 scheduled cases (72.1%). Justice H.T. Narendra Prasad in Court Hall 39 also maintained a strong hearing rate of 76.0% on 50 scheduled cases. In contrast, several single-judge benches with smaller dockets, including Justice S. Rachaiah (29 cases scheduled) and Justice S.R. Krishna Kumar (17 cases scheduled), recorded 0% hearing rates for the day.
